title: Make your own rules: demasiado, el agua, un / algún / ningún

cards.title: Make your own rules
cards.body: The course hasn't covered every detail, but it has given you the analytical tools to work out new patterns yourself as you practise and listen.

cards.title: demasiado = too (much / many)
cards.body: De más ('of more'): tengo cuatro de más = I have four too many. With a noun it agrees (demasiadas casas); with an adjective it doesn't (demasiado agresiva). Identifying the word type explains it.

cards.title: el agua: feminine but with el
cards.body: Two-syllable feminine words that start with a stressed a take el: el ala (wing), el agua (water), el aula (classroom). They stay feminine: el agua fría. Longer ones keep la: la alfombra, la almohada.

cards.title: uno → un, alguno → algún, ninguno → ningún
cards.body: Before a masculine noun they lose the final o. Feminine forms don't change: una, alguna, ninguna.

examples.en: I want one. / I don't want any.
a car / some car / no car
examples.es: un coche / algún coche / ningún coche

examples.en: a woman / some woman / no woman
examples.es: una mujer / alguna mujer / ninguna mujer

cards.title: Control the language, then live in it
cards.body: Analyse whatever you don't understand so it doesn't control you. Once the technical problems are solved, you can live freely in Spanish and become another version of yourself in it.
